about_blocks.text: EHN Guardians Nanaimo is an inpatient trauma and addiction centre for Canadian Armed Forces members, veterans, RCMP officers and other first responders. EHN Canada runs it at 2113 Boxwood Road in Nanaimo, on the same campus as EHN Edgewood Nanaimo. Guardians clients live in their own self-contained building, separate from civilian patients.
about_blocks.html: EHN Guardians Nanaimo is an inpatient trauma and addiction centre for Canadian Armed Forces members, veterans, RCMP officers and other first responders. EHN Canada runs it at 2113 Boxwood Road in Nanaimo, on the same campus as EHN Edgewood Nanaimo. Guardians clients live in their own self-contained building, separate from civilian patients.

about_blocks.text: There are two programs. The Vancouver Island Trauma, PTSD and Psychological Injury Inpatient Program runs seven weeks and is for people whose main problem is PTSD or an operational stress injury. The Vancouver Island Trauma, PTSD and Addiction Inpatient Program runs nine weeks and also treats alcohol and drug use. EHN says some clients stay longer when they need extended care.

about_blocks.text: Physicians and psychiatrists lead the care. Nurses are on site around the clock, and dedicated trauma staff are in the building 24/7. The therapies EHN names include cognitive processing therapy, prolonged exposure, EMDR, CBT, DBT and Internal Family Systems. Each client sees a primary counsellor at least once a week, and the rest of the day fills up with peer groups, trauma-sensitive yoga, therapeutic boxing, art therapy and gym time. Medically supervised detox and stabilization are part of admission when a client needs them.

about_blocks.text: Every room is private. Meals are served in the Bridges Dining Room, and clients can use the campus café, the gym, wooded walking trails and an outdoor labyrinth. EHN describes the centre as inclusive and culturally safe, with an Indigenous space, a 2SLGBTQIA+ friendly space and a multi-faith room.

about_blocks.text: You don't need a referral, but you do need to be a military member, veteran or first responder, or someone covered by presumptive PTSD or OSI legislation. The program pages also mention healthcare workers. EHN works with Veterans Affairs Canada, WorkSafeBC and RCMP Health Services, and private or group insurance can help too. Prices aren't published; admissions gives you a cost after a free assessment.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About EHN Guardians Nanaimo

faqs.question: Who can attend EHN Guardians Nanaimo?

answer_blocks.text: EHN Guardians Nanaimo is only for people in uniformed and protective roles: Canadian Armed Forces members, veterans, RCMP officers, municipal and provincial first responders, and others covered by presumptive PTSD or operational stress injury legislation. The program pages also list healthcare professionals. The main diagnosis has to relate to an operational stress injury, with or without a substance use problem.

The program pages also list healthcare professionals. The main diagnosis has to relate to an operational stress injury, with or without a substance use problem.

faqs.question: Is EHN Guardians Nanaimo the same as EHN Edgewood Nanaimo?

answer_blocks.text: No. Both are run by EHN Canada and share a campus on Boxwood Road in Nanaimo, but Guardians is a separate program for military, veterans and first responders. Guardians clients live in their own building away from civilian patients, while they can still use shared campus spaces like the dining room, café and gym.

faqs.question: How long are the programs at EHN Guardians Nanaimo?

answer_blocks.text: The trauma, PTSD and psychological injury program runs 7 weeks. The trauma, PTSD and addiction program, for people who also struggle with alcohol or drugs, runs 9 weeks. EHN says extended care is available for some clients.

faqs.question: How much does EHN Guardians Nanaimo cost?

answer_blocks.text: EHN does not publish prices for Guardians Nanaimo. The admissions team gives you a cost after a free assessment confirms the program fits. EHN says the cost depends on program length, clinical complexity and your needs.

faqs.question: Can Veterans Affairs, WorkSafeBC or the RCMP pay for treatment?

answer_blocks.text: Often, yes. EHN says it works with Veterans Affairs Canada, WorkSafeBC and RCMP Health Services, and that private and group health insurance may also be used. The admissions team checks your eligibility and handles the claims with you.

faqs.question: Does EHN Guardians Nanaimo offer medical detox?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Medically supervised detox and stabilization are part of admission when they are clinically needed. Nurses and counsellors are on site 24/7 and doctors are available.

faqs.question: Where is EHN Guardians Nanaimo and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: The centre is at 2113 Boxwood Road in central Nanaimo, on the east coast of Vancouver Island and about 10 minutes from the Departure Bay ferry terminal. From Vancouver it takes about three hours including the Horseshoe Bay ferry, and Victoria is roughly an hour and a half south by car.

faqs.question: What support is there after the program?

answer_blocks.text: After discharge you join a weekly therapy group with other alumni for one year. You also get lifelong membership in the EHN Canada Alumni Association, and aftercare and relapse prevention groups run both in person and online.
